Goblins: A relentless red swarm where dying Goblins are a resource, not a loss. Skirk Prospector sacrifices them for mana and Pashalik Mons turns each death into damage, while Siege-Gang Commander and Sulfuric Vortex push the last points through. Pick this if you love flooding the board and attacking without mercy.
Aristocrats/Sacrifice: Every creature you control is fuel for something better. Yawgmoth, Thran Physician turns them into cards and shrinking blockers while Oversold Cemetery keeps handing the fodder back, so the long attrition war is never close. For players who enjoy squeezing advantage out of every death.
Threshold: Seven cards in the graveyard and the whole deck levels up. Cheap self-mill and cycling switch on Mystic Enforcer and Werebear well ahead of schedule, and Glory shields the team from the yard you just filled. Rewarding if you like decks that quietly power up and then take over.
Enchantress: Cast an enchantment, draw a card, repeat until the game is over. Mesa Enchantress and Zur the Enchanter bury opponents in card advantage while Sylvan Library and Mystic Remora keep your hand full. For players who want to build a machine and win on sheer resources.
Tokens / Go-Wide: One creature at a time was never the plan. Saproling Symbiosis and Battle Screech flood the board, Divine Sacrament makes the whole team lethal, and Opposition can tap the opponent out of the game entirely. Perfect if you like big boards and swinging with everything.
Reanimator / Cheat Big Creatures: Skip the mana cost and drop something game-ending far too early. Entomb and Gamble load the graveyard, then Chainer and Dread Return haul the monsters back while Sneak Attack slams them straight from hand. For players who want explosive, do-something-huge turns.
Madness / Discard Value: Throwing cards away is how this deck pays for things. Discard outlets like Aquamoeba and Zombie Infestation cast your madness spells at a discount, turning the bin into a weapon. Great for players who enjoy clever, cost-cutting sequencing.
Cycling: A deck that never floods, because every dead card becomes a new one. Lightning Rift and Invigorating Boon turn each cycled card into free damage or growth, so there is always something to do. Ideal if you like consistency and steady incremental value.
Storm / High Tide Combo: One enormous turn, assembled out of almost nothing. High Tide and free untappers build a mountain of mana, then Grapeshot or Empty the Warrens converts it into a kill. For players who love chaining spells toward a lethal finish.
Blink / ETB Value: Good enter-the-battlefield triggers are far too good to use only once. Momentary Blink and Whitemane Lion re-trigger Flametongue Kavu and Man-o'-War until the opponent has nothing left. Satisfying if you like value engines and an answer for everything.
Prison / Stax Control: A deck built to make attacking you a bad idea. No Mercy and Windborn Muse punish aggression, Icy Manipulator taps whatever is left, and Wrath of God resets anything that slips through. For players who enjoy saying no and winning slowly.
Artifacts: Trinkets that quietly add up to an engine. Urza, Lord High Artificer turns your artifacts into a giant Construct and a pile of mana, powering out payoffs like Triskelion. For players who like combo-adjacent value engines.
Lifegain: Gain enough life and it stops being defence. Congregate, Lyra Dawnbringer and Spirit Link push the total somewhere silly, then Test of Endurance and Serra Avatar cash it in. For players who like outlasting opponents and flipping defence into offence.
Lands-Matter / Ramp: Every land drop should do something. Exploration and Tatyova, Benthic Druid turn extra lands into cards and life, while Terravore grows into a finisher off the graveyard. For players who enjoy accelerating ahead and grinding out value.
+1/+1 Counters: One creature, counters piling up, until it simply ends the game. Forgotten Ancient hoards them and hands them to Triskelion or the Phantoms, and proliferate keeps them coming. For players who like building a single unstoppable threat.
Marit Lage (Dark Depths): A 20/20 flying indestructible token, out of nowhere. Crop Rotation fetches Dark Depths and green ramp clears its ice counters for a sudden knockout. A high-risk, high-reward pick for players who love a flashy one-card haymaker.
Five-Color Legends: Play every splashy gold bomb in the cube, all in one deck. Lair lands, Gemstone Mine and Birds of Paradise make the mana work, and Legacy Weapon becomes a repeatable removal engine. For players who want the greediest pile at the table.
Mono-Color Big Mana (Gauntlet): Commit to one colour and get paid twice for every land. Gauntlet of Power supercharges your basics until firebreathers like Nantuko Shade and Shivan Dragon grow completely out of control. For players who like going tall rather than wide.
Untap Pinger Engine (Crab Gun): Two cards turn Horseshoe Crab into a machine gun. Hermetic Study makes each untap a ping, Quicksilver Dagger makes it draw a card, and Opposition locks down the board instead. A puzzle-piece build-around for players who love repeatable engines.
